1. Start ASE2000 in Task Mode
2. Create Modbus RTU definition with Digital and Analog points
3. Start RTU Simulation
4. Start another ASE2000 instance as Master Simulation
5. Send Read Coil Status command
Expected Results: ASE2000 should automatically extend the Point List for digital points to the next multiple of 8 (i.e., 8 points displayed when 5 are defined). This behavior aligns with the Modbus RTU protocol requirement for byte-packing (8 bits per data byte).

Have multiple users.
Have different user.config files in different user profiles.

1. Upgrade/Downgrade ASE2000. Open ASE2000.

Expected Results: Verify that after upgrade/downgrade the specific user configuration settings of the signed in user is only used by the application for migration even if upgrade/downgrade is done in another user profile.

Summary: When an IEC104 Master exchange configured with a specific Channel, it should use the channel’s Host/Port for connection and message routing, overriding the global Host/Port - TC1
Actions:
1. Open two instances of ASE2000 - configure one as Master and another as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol.
2. Start the RTU active on "127.0.0.1:2404".
3. In Master, configure global host and port as machine IP and 2404 respectively.
4. Configure channel of any Master exchange to 127.0.0.1:2404 and initiate that exchange.
5. Observe the communication.
Expected Results: 1. Verify that TCP connection is initiated to 127.0.0.1:2404 (channel config) and not to the global Host (machine ip).

Summary:

Summary:
To verify the behavior of an Interrogation request in IEC104 Exchange Mode where,
Master Interrogates with COA X,
with no points configured in the RTU.
Common Address Format = Unstructured.
Preconditions: Have two instances - Master and RTU, of ASE2000 open, in Exchange Mode, for IEC104 protocol.
Actions:
Configure the Master as following:
StartDT | Frequency = 0 | Flags = Display, Transmit
Interrogation | COA = X | Frequency = 0 | Flags = Display, Transmit
--------------------------------------------
Configure the RTU as following: Default
--------------------------------------------
Start the RTU, Play the Master.
Expected Results:
The requests and responses must follow the following order:
-> StartDT ACT
<- StartDT CON
-> Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation | COA = X
<- Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation Confirmation | COA = X
<- Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation Termination | COA = X
Remarks: Here, X is an integer in the valid range; 1 to 65535

Summary: IEC104 Master-RTU connection using channel configured endpoint (IP/Port), overriding the Master’s global Host/Port.
Actions:
1. Open two instances of ASE2000 - configure one as Master and another as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol.
2. In RTU, configure global host and port as 127.0.0.1 and 2404 respectively. Start the RTU.
3. In Master, configure global host and port with machine IP and 2404 respectively.
4. Configure channel of Startdt Act exchange as "127.0.0.1:2404" and initiate that exchange.
5. Observe the communication.
Expected Results: 1. Verify that Startdt Act request is being send to and Startdt Con is received from 127.0.0.1:2404 (channel config) and not to the global Host (machine ip).

Summary: IEC104 Master uses the channel configured endpoint (IP/Port) to establish IEC 104 communication across two machines, overriding the Master’s global Host/Port.

Actions:
1. Open an ASE2000 instance as RTU in Exchange Mode with IEC104 protocol using machine IP and 2404 as global Host and Port. Start RTU.

3. In Master, configure channel of Startdt Act exchange as "<RTU Machine IP>:2404" and initiate that exchange.

Summary:
To verify the behaviour of an Interrogation request in IEC104 Exchange Mode where,
Master Interrogates with COA X,
with a point configured in the RTU with COA *.
Common Address Format = Unstructured.
Preconditions: Have two instances - Master and RTU, of ASE2000 open, in Exchange Mode, for IEC104 protocol.
Actions:
Configure the Master as following:
StartDT | Frequency = 0 | Flags = Display, Transmit
Interrogation | COA = X | Frequency = 0 | Flags = Display, Transmit
--------------------------------------------
Configure the RTU as following:
M_Point A | COA = * | Flags = Display, Interrogation | Any number of IOAs
--------------------------------------------
Start the RTU, Play the Master.
Expected Results:
The requests and responses must follow the following order:
-> StartDT ACT
<- StartDT CON
-> Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation | COA = X
<- Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation Confirmation | COA = X
<- Type ID = t | COT = Interrogated by general interrogation | COA = X | All the IOAs
<- Type ID = 100 | COT = Activation Termination | COA = X

Summary: To verify that only the Master sends a TestFR ACT on an idle line when T1, T2, T3 are configured with same values on both Master and RTU in Task Mode
Preconditions: Have two instances of ASE2000 open in Task Mode as Master and RTU configured for IEC104.
Actions:
1. In Tools -> Properties -> IEC104 -> Options of both Master and RTU, enter the same values for T1, T2, T3 (Say, 15, 10, 10).
2. Start the RTU, Connect the Master
3. Send Once from the Master: StartDT
4. Wait for the T3 (10 Sec) to elapse
Expected Results: Once the T3 is elapsed, only the Master must send a TestFR ACT to which the RTU must respond with a TestFR CON. The same behaviour must be observed at every iteration of T3 elapse.

Summary: Delayed RTU follow-up received after a newer master request becomes active is routed to the current active master
Preconditions:
1. Requires 2 machines - M1 as splitter and RTU; M2 as master
2. Config.csv contains a row:
<M1 IP>,40001;40011,<M1 IP>,41001
Actions:
1. Start dummy RTU with delayed response and delayed follow-up on M1 at <M1 IP>:41001 using command :
python dummy_rtu.py --host <M1 IP> --port 41001 --response-hex "10 10" --echo-request-in-response --unsol-hex "AA BB CC DD" --unsol-after-first-req-ms 4000
2. Start TCP Splitter.
3. Start Master A on M2 at <M1 IP>:40001 using command :
python dummy_master.py --host <M1 IP> --port 40001 --name A --frame "0|01 01|ReqA" --keep-open 20
4. Before A’s delayed follow-up arrives, start Master B on M2 at <M1 IP>:40011 using command :
python dummy_master.py --host <M1 IP> --port 40011 --name B --keep-open 20
Expected Results:
1. Master A receives its first response alone "10 10 01 01".
2. Master B receives the second response of Master A, "20 20 01 01"

Summary: Stale disconnected master must not receive or leak fallback RTU traffic to another connected master
Preconditions:
1. Requires 2 machines - M1 as splitter and RTU; M2 as master
2. Config.csv contains a row:
<M1 IP>,40001;40011,<M1 IP>,41001
Actions:
1. Start dummy RTU using delayed unsolicited configuration on M1 at <M1 IP>:41001 using command :
python dummy_rtu.py --host <M1 IP> --port 41001 --response-hex "11 22" --unsol-hex "AA BB CC DD" --unsol-after-first-req-ms 2
2. Start TCP Splitter.
3. Start Master A on M2 at <M1 IP>:40001 using command :
python dummy_master.py --host <M1 IP> --port 40001 --name A --frame "0|01 02|ReqA" --close-after-send 10
4. Allow Master A to receive its response, then disconnect.
5. Start Master B without sending any request on M2 at <M1 IP>:40011 using command :
python dummy_master.py --host <M1 IP> --port 40011 --name B --keep-open 60
Expected Results:
1. Master B must not receive unsolicited frame "AA BB CC DD"
2. Splitter must not leak stale fallback routing from disconnected Master A into Master B.
